kernel: twoWayScan<opType> (device function inlined into vhgw_horiz<opType> and vhgw_vert<opType>, 4 kernel instances: opType 0/1 x horiz/vert)

sites.source: opArray[tid + selSize - 1] = elementOp<opType>(opArray[tid + selSize - 1], opArray[tid + selSize - 1 - offset]);  (statement spans L94-L95; the store is attributed to L94)
opArray[tid + selSize - 1 - offset]  (operand of the same statement; ld.shared.u8)

thread_pair_example: driver ./main 64 64 192 192 1 (selSize = 64 -> blocks of 64 threads = 2 warps), vhgw_horiz, any block, offset = 1: thread 31 (warp 0) writes opArray[31 + 64 - 1] = opArray[94] (L94) while thread 32 (warp 1) reads opArray[32 + 64 - 1 - 1] = opArray[94] (L95); the barrier is only at the end of the iteration (L100). Mirrored pair in the reverse scan (L98, not listed as a site): thread 34 writes opArray[34] while thread 33 reads opArray[33 + 1] = opArray[34]. vhgw_vert has the same pair with threadIdx.y as tid.
class_reason: plain unsigned char accesses in dynamic shared memory by different warps with no barrier between the read of an iteration and the in-place write by another thread: DR. Single-byte accesses; the conflicting addresses are identical bytes.
buggy_expected: the pair (write L94 vs read L95, plus the reverse-scan pair L98 vs L98) is reported as DR (RAW/WAR across warps on opArray bytes), in all four kernel instances; for selSize <= 32 only an intra-warp lock-step pair would remain (not exercised by this driver).

fixed.reason: the fix (7be8747e) rewrites the loop into a read phase into registers (L102-L103), __syncthreads (L105), then a write phase (L107-L108), with a __syncthreads (L100) at the start of every iteration, so no read of opArray in an iteration is concurrent with a write of the same iteration (verify.expected_report_fixed).

sass_notes: sm_89 SASS of vhgw_horiz<1> from the shipped build (sassline.sh): L95 LDS.U8 R2,[R11+-0x1] (0x0260) and LDS.U8 R3,[R11+UR4] (0x0270), L94 STS.U8 [R11+-0x1] (0x02b0), reverse scan L98 LDS.U8 [R9] (0x02c0), LDS.U8 [R9+UR5] (0x02d0), STS.U8 [R9] (0x0320), BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x0 at 0x0330 (L100); all plain LDS.U8/STS.U8, no .STRONG token, no WARPSYNC anywhere in the kernels. vhgw_vert has the same structure (L95 0x0280/0x0290, L94 0x02d0, L98 0x02e0-0x0340, BAR 0x0350). The fixed build: LDS L102/L103 (0x02a0-0x02d0 in vhgw_vert), BAR.SYNC at L105 (0x0310), STS at L107/L108 (0x0330/0x0350), BAR.SYNC at L100 (0x0250).

open_questions: Accesses are single bytes: a detector with word-granular shadow memory may merge neighbouring bytes written by different threads into extra (false) pairs; the true conflicts are on identical byte addresses (verify.notes).
The driver is 192x192 (reporter: 512x512); the 128x128 image prints FAIL in both variants (the app's own result check depends on the border), 130..256 PASS.
